author: nonretail_writer
central_thesis: At 00:00 UTC on 23 February 2022, Russia's recognition of the Donetsk and Luhansk 'republics' and the order to send troops into them had turned the Ukraine overhang into a priced energy-and-margin shock: the S&P 500 confirmed a correction, Brent closed at 96.84 USD/bbl and Dutch TTF jumped +8.17%, Germany halted Nord Stream 2 certification, and the first US/UK/EU sanctions were calibrated (Russia's largest banks escaped the UK round). The Fed's March lift-off is intact and the curve is bear flattening, so the market prices a stagflationary supply premium rather than a financial-system shock. The book favours energy, food/fertiliser, Russia-sensitive metals and defence producers and intermediate Treasuries over long-duration growth, Hong Kong-listed China internet and Polish banks; a full-scale invasion is treated only as a pending risk, never as a fact.
sources_policy: Only the 2022-02-23 frozen feed (via tools/digest.py and direct ID lookup) and the 2022-02-23 market card (via tools/showcard.py) were used; reference voice excerpts were read for voice and depth only. No other date's feed, card, spec, draft or note, no specs/, retail_drafts/, notes/retail_* or audit/independent_* files, and no web access. Every cited claim was checked against its own-date title wording, outlet metadata and timestamp; every number against the card or a headline cited in the same part. Windows respected by meaning: company news/previews within seven days (from 2022-02-16), company results within fourteen (from 2022-02-09), macro releases/policy baselines within thirty-five (from 2022-01-19). Previews are used only as pending events. Market figures carry '(Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-22)', '(US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-22)' or, for crypto, '(Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-22)'; curve wording is the card's ('positively sloped', 'bear flattening (both up, 2Y up more)'). No numeric spot-FX; currency direction only from dated reporting. Biden's 'beginning invasion' is reported only as his characterisation of the Donbas deployment. Period identities used: Meta Platforms (FB), Raytheon Technologies (RTX), Mercedes-Benz Group. No Polish company appears in the Sector Deep Dive. 260 distinct IDs cited, none more than twice; the previous writer's stopped draft was re-verified claim by claim and rewritten rather than copied.
